st: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain. Put it in a pot with the coconut milk, water, ginger, pandan and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes. Rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, then peel and halve them.
Fry the anchovies in [[0.25 cup]] hot oil for 2 minutes until crisp. Drain, then fry the peanuts for 1 minute and drain.
Blend the soaked chiles, shallots and garlic into a paste.
Fry the paste in [[0.25 cup]] oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until the oil separates and it darkens.
Stir in the tamarind, sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook for 3 minutes. This is the sambal.
Serve the rice with sambal, egg, cucumber, peanuts and anchovies on the side.

ing: kerisik, or toasted shredded coconut ground
st: Blend the chiles, shallots, ginger, galangal, garlic and turmeric to a smooth paste, adding a splash of coconut milk if needed.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the paste for 8 minutes until fragrant and darker.
Add the beef and stir to coat. Cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the lemongrass, lime leaves, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and palm sugar. Bring to a gentle boil.
Simmer uncovered on low for 2 hours, stirring every 15 minutes, until the sauce thickens and the beef is tender.
Stir in the toasted coconut. Keep cooking for 30 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and dark and the oil shows on top.
Taste and adjust salt. Remove the lemongrass. Serve with steamed rice.

ing: cut in 2 inch pieces, or green onion
st: Mix the dark soy, light soy, oyster sauce, chili paste and white pepper in a small bowl.
Heat a wok or large skillet on the highest heat until smoking. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Add the sausage if using and the garlic and stir for 15 seconds, then add the shrimp and cook for 1 minute until pink. Move to a plate.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and the noodles. Pour in the sauce and toss for 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and lightly charred.
Push the noodles aside. Add the rest of the oil and the eggs. Scramble until almost set, then mix into the noodles.
Return the shrimp. Add the bean sprouts and chives and toss for 1 minute.
Serve immediately on a hot plate while it still has wok flavor.
Simmer the shrimp shells in [[5 cups]] water for 15 minutes. Strain and keep the stock.
Blend the chiles, shallots, garlic, ginger, turmeric and shrimp paste to a paste.
Fry the paste in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes until fragrant and the oil rises.
Add the lemongrass and stock. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the coconut milk, fish sauce and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Simmer gently 5 minutes without a hard boil.
Add the shrimp and tofu puffs and cook for 3 minutes until the shrimp are pink.
Cook the noodles per package, drain and divide into bowls with bean sprouts.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles and serve with lime.
Blend the lemongrass, shallots, garlic, turmeric, coriander, soy sauce, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tbsp]] oil to a paste.
Toss the chicken with the paste. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour or overnight.
Soak the skewers in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
For the sauce, fry the chili paste in [[1 tbsp]] oil for 2 minutes. Add the peanuts, coconut milk, water, tamarind and [[1 tbsp]] sugar.
Simmer the sauce for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick. Add water if too thick.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers.
Grill on a hot grill or broiler for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked to 165°F (74°C).
Serve hot with the peanut sauce, cucumber and onion.
Mix the flour, sugar and salt in a bowl. Add the egg, milk, [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and the water.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Coat each well with oil and rest in a covered dish for 1 hour.
Oil the counter well. Flatten a ball and stretch it very thin with oiled hands until nearly see-through.
Drizzle with melted butter, then fold the edges to the center to make a square, or roll it up like a rope and coil it.
Rest the coiled dough for 15 minutes, then flatten gently into a round.
Cook in a hot skillet with a little oil for 2 minutes per side until golden and flaky.
Clap the hot roti between your hands to fluff the layers. Serve with curry or dal.
Rub the chicken all over with [[1 tsp]] salt. Stuff the cavity with the ginger slices, green onions and [[2 cloves]] garlic.
Bring the water to a boil in a pot just big enough to hold the chicken. Lower in the chicken, return to a simmer, then turn the heat off and cover for 50 minutes. The thigh must reach 165°F (74°C).
Move the chicken to a bowl of ice water for 10 minutes to firm up the skin. Keep the poaching broth. Rub with sesame oil.
Mince [[2 cloves]] garlic and fry in the oil for 1 minute. Add the rice and fry for 2 minutes.
Add [[3 cups]] of the broth and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook covered on low for 15 minutes, rest 10 minutes.
Blend the chiles, the remaining garlic, the grated ginger, soy sauce, vinegar and [[3 tbsp]] broth for the chili sauce.
Carve the chicken and serve with rice, cucumber, chili sauce and a small bowl of hot broth.

ing: green mustard greens or choy sum
st: Boil the potato cubes in salted water for 10 minutes until tender, then drain.
Rinse the noodles in hot water to loosen them and drain well.
Mix the soy sauce, chili paste and ketchup in a small bowl.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a wok. Fry the tofu for 3 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Add [[1 tbsp]] oil, the garlic and shallot and cook for 30 seconds. Add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Push the noodles aside. Crack in the eggs and scramble for 1 minute, then stir through.
Add the potato, tofu, greens and bean sprouts. Toss for 2 minutes until just wilted. Season with salt.
Serve hot with lime wedges.
Steep the butterfly pea flowers in the hot water for 10 minutes, then strain and keep the blue water.
Cook the rice in the blue water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt: bring to a boil, cover and cook on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes.
Rub the fish with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the lemongrass and oil.
Grill or pan-fry the fish for 4 minutes per side until it flakes. Flake the meat apart.
Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden. Mix it with the flaked fish for the topping.
Blanch the long beans in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Toss the herbs, shallots, cucumber, beans and bean sprouts with the lime juice.
Mound the blue rice on plates and surround with the fish-coconut mix and the fresh salad.

ing: stemmed, soaked in hot water 15 minutes
st: Drain the soaked chiles and discard the water.
Toast the shrimp paste in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant, if using.
Blend the dried chiles, fresh chiles, shallots, garlic and shrimp paste into a fairly smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-low heat. Add the paste carefully and fry for 12 minutes, stirring often.
Cook until the oil separates and the color deepens to a rich dark red.
Stir in the sugar, tamarind and [[0.75 tsp]] salt. Cook for 3 minutes.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

ing: mung bean starch or tapioca starch
st: Blend the pandan leaves with [[1 cup]] water and strain well to get green juice.
Whisk the rice flour, starch, salt and the pandan juice in a saucepan until smooth.
Cook over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, stirring non-stop, until it thickens into a thick green paste.
Press the hot paste through a colander with large holes into a bowl of ice water, to make short noodles. Let them firm up for 10 minutes.
Simmer the palm sugar with [[0.5 cup]] water for 5 minutes until syrupy, then cool.
Drain the green noodles well in a sieve.
Put red beans and cendol noodles into 4 bowls and pile with shaved ice.
Drizzle with the coconut milk and palm sugar syrup. Eat right away.
Bring the water to a boil in a small pot.
Add the tea bags and simmer for 5 minutes for a very strong brew.
Remove the tea bags, pressing out the liquid.
Put the condensed milk and evaporated milk into a heatproof pitcher or tall mug. Add sugar if wanted.
Pour in the hot tea and stir to combine.
Pour the tea back and forth between two pitchers from a height of about a foot, 6 to 8 times, until frothy and a bit cooler.
Divide into two glasses and drink while hot and foamy.
